issuing_body: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Minnesota
title: DOJ Fraud Division and District of Minnesota announce benefits-fraud enforcement surge
notes: Source-level capture from official government release on November 1, 2026. Multiple legal stages are separately described and must not be collapsed. Source status follows existing live corpus records.
supports: DOJ states that 13 defendants were charged, convicted or sentenced between September 30 and October 30, involving nearly $83 million in alleged or proven intended losses and about $29.1 million of fraud in newly charged cases; these are mixed measures, not amounts collected.
Shaakir Mohamud Ibrahim was indicted September 29 in a Feeding Our Future matter alleging more than $1.1 million in reimbursements.

Emily Marice Ravits and Feisal Mohamed Elmi were indicted October 22 in EIDBI-related matters; Habiba Mohamed was charged by information October 29; Faiza Osman Ahmed and Jama Yusuf Mohamod were indicted October 28 in Medicaid matters.
Ahmed Abdul Razaq Al Obaidi and Muhammad Abdullah Kahn were charged by complaint on October 21 in an alleged SNAP-benefit trafficking matter.

A jury convicted Muna Wais Fidhin on October 21 of three wire-fraud, four federal-programs-bribery and two money-laundering counts involving sites sponsored by Feeding Our Future and Partners in Nutrition.
Nicole Lee Slegers and Shaun Hubert Slegers pleaded guilty October 28 to conspiracy to commit wire fraud concerning deceased Medicaid recipients' estates.

Salim Ahmed Said was sentenced October 28 to 360 months in prison and DOJ described over $44 million in fraud proceeds facilitated; DOJ did not independently certify a collected restitution amount in this release.
Said Farah was sentenced October 30 to 78 months and a $40,000 fine in a separate juror-bribery matter.
DOJ reports an October 19 civil forfeiture action concerning three properties valued at about $519,000, encumbered by lis pendens.
does_not_support: Any latest comprehensive count of Feeding Our Future charged, convicted or sentenced defendants.
An additional $83 million of proven losses or recovered funds.
That civil forfeiture property has been liquidated or transferred.
A signed judgment setting Said's precise restitution obligation.
